rationale: Verb of inquiry opening the disciple's question. Possibly Lyc form related to ⲱⲛⲧ 'ask' (cf. accumulated ⲱⲛⲧ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗) or ⲛⲟⲩⲉ 'draw near' in inquiry-sense. Captures the structural opening 'an inquiry concerning this saying...' typical of Kephalaia chapter heads.

Preposition ⲁ 'to/in' + ⲙ̄ 'the' + ⲙⲟⲩⲉⲓⲩⲉ 'waters' (Lyc plural of ⲙⲟⲩ). Standard Lycopolitan compound for 'into/in the waters.' Recurs throughout this kephalaion as the locus of the reflective mystery.

Qualitative form, possibly Lyc ⲉⲣⲍⲣⲁⲕ from ϩⲣⲟⲕ 'be calm, still' (cf. ⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧϩ 'stillness' in glossary). Describes the reflected face fixed motionless below the surface. Alternative ⲉⲣⲏⲕ 'as far as' less probable.

proposed_english: the man of heaven / man from above
rationale: Compound: ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'man' + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲧⲡⲉ 'heaven, above.' The 'man of heaven' is the parable-figure whose reflection in water signifies the cosmic Call/Answer mystery. Distinct from the technical 'First Man' (ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ) which is mentioned later as the recipient of the Call.

Reflexive verbal phrase: ⲃⲓ (from ϥⲓ 'lift') + ⲭⲱϩ (= ϫⲱϥ reflexive 'himself') + ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward.' Parallels line 15's ⲛⲁⲭϥ̄ ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛ̄ 'cast himself down.' The upward-self-lifting man generates the parallel Answer-mystery.
Greek loanword σημαίνει 'signifies, gives signs.' Standard Greek-Coptic exegetical-correspondential term in Manichaean usage. Confirms the systematic-typological mode of this kephalaion.

proposed_english: that I may instruct you / teach you
rationale: Future causative ⲧⲁⲧ-ⲥⲃⲱ-ⲕ 'that-I-shall-cause-you-to-be-taught.' From ⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching' (per terminology guide). Standard Manichaean teacher-formula 'hear, that I may teach you.'
Plural ⲧⲃⲛⲁⲩⲉ from ⲧⲃⲛⲏ 'cattle, beast' with article ⲡⲁ- 'that of.' The face of cattle reflected in water alongside the face of men and of trees — a cosmographic triad of mirrored kinds.
Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲁϣⲓⲁⲉ from ⲁϣⲁⲓ 'be many.' Paired with ⲟⲩϭⲣⲟ 'victory' as the dual character of the Call's descent into the lower cosmoi.
